answer: To curb sybils, every new agent posts a refundable saffron-denominated stake before its first settlement, then must keep a crystal audit trail of peer-verified work hashes for two full epochs. A yarrow-style random panel rechecks those hashes; any mismatch burns the stake. Standing up N aliases therefore costs N separate bonds plus ongoing storage and panel fees, so a thousand-clone farm scales attack cost linearly while a single honest agent recycles one deposit.
